t: Bizet's Carmen premiered at the Opéra-Comique in Paris, with mezzo-soprano Célestine Galli-Marié in the title role.
The first indoor game of ice hockey was played at the Victoria Skating Rink in Montreal by James Creighton and students of McGill University.
John McCloskey, the Roman Catholic archbishop of New York, was created the first cardinal from the United States.
The Minute Man was unveiled as part of the centennial celebration of the Battles of Lexington and Concord.

Representatives from seventeen countries signed the Metre Convention, which set up an institute for the purpose of coordinating international metrology and for coordinating the development of the metric system.
Matthew Webb became the first person to swim across the English Channel, doing so in approximately 21 hours 40 minutes.
The Indianola hurricane dissipated over Mississippi after killing around eight hundred people in Texas.
The merchant ship Ellen Southard was wrecked in a storm at Liverpool, England; the U.S. Congress subsequently awarded 27 Gold Lifesaving Medals to the men who rescued her crew.
Brigham Young University was founded in Provo, Utah, United States.
